technical_and_design_decisions: For U1 (gpfdist sink): Refactor existing Spring XD module code (from gpfdist repository) into the core Spring XD module structure. Integrate with the project-reactor based data pipeline architecture. Maintain compatibility with existing GPDB/HAWQ writing capabilities.

For U2 (Centralized Module Registry): Implement a new `ModuleRegistry` implementation that uses Git (specifically GitHub) as the backend storage. Use JGit library for Git operations. The REST API for module upload/deploy will interact with this new registry.

For U3 (Rabbit benchmark): Design a benchmark suite using JMeter or a similar tool. The benchmark will simulate increasing load by adding more simulated xd-container nodes (threads) publishing messages to a RabbitMQ instance hosted on Rackspace infrastructure.

For U4 (Flo parser error reporting): Enhance the existing Flo parser endpoint logic to capture, structure, and propagate more detailed error information (e.g., specific syntax errors, line numbers) back to the client in a standardized format (likely JSON).

For U5 (Secure Mail source): Extend the existing `mail` source module configuration to support a new property (`java-mail-properties`) that accepts a reference to a Spring `java.util.Properties` bean. This bean will contain the standard JavaMail SSL/TLS properties (e.g., `mail.imaps.ssl.enable`). Leverage Spring Integration's existing `MailReceivingChannelAdapter` and its property-passing mechanisms.

For U6 (HDFS as default module registry): Modify the module upload process (both via `xd-shell` and REST API) to target HDFS as the storage location for custom module JARs. Update the deployment logic to fetch modules from HDFS. Remove the `custom-modules.zip` packaging step from the YARN distribution build process.

For U7 (Shell auto-configuration): Implement a startup initialization mechanism for `xd-shell`. This will involve: 1) Checking for a well-known configuration file location (e.g., `/etc/springxd/conf/xd-shell.init`). 2) Parsing and executing the commands within that file (e.g., `server config ...`, `hadoop config ...`) automatically upon shell launch, before presenting the user prompt.

For U8 (Graceful stream shutdown): Modify the stream undeployment process to implement a 'drain' phase. This involves: 1) Sending a signal to the stream's source to stop accepting new messages. 2) Allowing in-flight messages already in the pipeline (channels, queues) to be fully processed and delivered to the sink. 3) Implementing a configurable timeout to prevent indefinite waiting. 4) Only after the drain completes (or times out) will the stream's components be destroyed.
assumptions: The development team has prior experience with the Spring XD codebase, Spring Integration, and the respective technologies mentioned (Project Reactor, JGit, JavaMail, RabbitMQ, HDFS, YARN).
The existing code for the gpfdist module (in the spring-xd-modules repository) is available and its functionality is well-understood.
A working development and integration testing environment is available, including access to a Hadoop cluster (HDFS/YARN), a RabbitMQ instance, and a sample GPDB/HAWQ database for U1 and U3.
Existing unit and integration tests for the affected modules (e.g., mail source, Flo parser, module deployment) exist and can be extended.

The scope is limited to the implementation of the features described in the user stories. This includes necessary refactoring, configuration changes, and writing of unit/integration tests. It excludes extensive performance tuning beyond the baseline measurement for U3.
For U7, the auto-configuration file format will be the same as the manual script file format, and the shell's existing `script` command parser will be reused.

For U8, the 'graceful shutdown' is scoped to the stream's data flow (messages in channels/queues). It does not include transaction management or guaranteed delivery across external systems that are already unreachable.

activities.activity_description: Move gpfdist sink code from the spring-xd-modules repository into the core Spring XD module structure. Refactor it to use the project-reactor based pipeline. Adjust package names, update internal references, and ensure it compiles and passes unit tests within the core project.

Develop a new `ModuleRegistry` interface implementation that uses JGit to interact with a GitHub repository. Implement methods for deploying modules (committing and pushing JAR files), retrieving modules, and listing modules. Integrate this new registry into the module upload REST endpoint and the deployment service. Write unit and integration tests.

Design a benchmark test plan to measure throughput and latency as simulated xd-container nodes are added. Set up a script/tool (e.g., JMeter) to publish messages to a RabbitMQ instance on Rackspace. Execute the benchmark for varying node counts, collect metrics (throughput, latency percentiles, CPU/memory usage on the RabbitMQ server), and produce a summary report.

Modify the Flo parser endpoint(s) to catch parsing exceptions in a more granular way. Implement logic to extract detailed error information (line number, column, expected token, actual token) from the parser's exception hierarchy. Structure this information into a standard error response object (JSON) and ensure it is returned to the client. Update or add tests for the new error paths.

activities.activity_name: Add Secure IMAP/SMTP Support to Mail Source (U5)
activities.activity_description: Extend the mail source module configuration XML schema (or bean definition parser) to accept a `java-mail-properties` attribute. Update the module's runtime logic to retrieve the referenced `Properties` bean and merge it with the adapter's configuration. Test with sample SSL properties for both IMAP and SMTP protocols.

activities.activity_name: Default Custom Module Registry to HDFS (U6)
activities.activity_description: Modify the module deployment logic to use HDFS as the default storage location. Update the `xd-shell` 'module upload' command and the corresponding REST API handler to write module JARs to a designated HDFS directory. Update the container deployment process to fetch modules from HDFS. Remove the `custom-modules.zip` artifact from the build scripts and YARN distribution configuration.

Implement an initialization hook in `xd-shell` that looks for a configuration file (e.g., `/etc/springxd/conf/xd-shell.init`) at startup. If found, the shell will automatically parse and execute the commands in the file before presenting the user prompt. This reuses the existing `script` command execution engine. Add unit tests for the file detection and parsing logic.

Modify the stream undeployment logic to implement a drain phase. Before destroying a stream's components: 1) Send a stop signal to the stream's source. 2) Allow a configurable timeout (default e.g., 30 seconds) for in-flight messages in the stream's internal channels and any associated message channels to be processed and delivered to the sink. 3) Log the drain progress and completion/timeout. Write integration tests that verify a message sent just before undeployment is fully processed.
